high.title: Gold Closes Higher Amid Uncertainties Over US-Iran Negotiations Resumption
high.summary: Gold futures closed higher on Friday as investors weighed new signals from Iran regarding resumption of negotiations with the US for an agreement to end the Middle East war, amid prolonged uncertainties. The market also evaluated comments from Federal Reserve officials about interest rate trajectory. On Comex, June gold closed up 0.32% at $4,644.50 per troy ounce, while silver rose 3.29% to $75.951 per ounce. However, for the week, metals fell 2% and 0.6% respectively. Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated that Tehran remains open to diplomacy with the US, provided Washington changes its "expansionist stance" and "threatening rhetoric." This geopolitical premium remains crucial for emerging markets like Brazil, as risk-on/risk-off sentiment directly impacts BRL flows and Brazilian asset prices. Higher gold prices typically signal continued safe-haven demand, which could pressure risk assets including Brazilian equities and bonds while supporting USD strength against BRL.

medium.title: Polymarket: Futures Contracts Expose Market Skepticism and Keep Geopolitical Premium 'On the Table'; See How to Position
medium.summary: Despite Iran's new proposal to the US including reopening the Strait of Hormuz, Polymarket futures contracts show extreme skepticism with less than 1% probability assigned to reopening by April 30, with over $31 million at stake. Contracts for definitive peace and nuclear agreements also show 1% probability with $66 million and $2 million in bets respectively. This persistent geopolitical risk premium continues to influence global risk appetite, maintaining pressure on emerging market assets including Brazilian bonds and equities.

medium.title: Trump Says He's Not Satisfied with Iran: 'We'll See What Happens with Negotiations'
medium.summary: President Trump expressed dissatisfaction with Iran after phone conversations with Persian leadership, stating Iran's government is fragmented and leadership is confused with tremendous disagreement. He mentioned they were close to an agreement but nuclear weapons supporters derailed talks. This continued geopolitical uncertainty maintains risk-off sentiment that typically pressures emerging market currencies like BRL and supports safe-haven assets over Brazilian bonds and equities.
